title.zh: 井陉口前，那条没人听的计
title.en: At Jingxing Pass: The Plan Nobody Heeded

dek.zh: 讲这场以少胜多的仗，可以只讲赢家的招数；这篇想说的是另一件事：一条被否决的建议，和赢家打赢之后怎样对待提建议的人。
dek.en: A battle won against the odds can be told through the winner's tricks alone. This one is about something else: a proposal that was rejected, and how the winner treated the man who made it after the fighting stopped.

heading.zh: 开战之前，一条建议被否了
heading.en: Before the battle, a proposal is turned down

paras.zh: 韩信和张耳带着数万人，准备东下井陉去打赵国；赵王歇和成安君陈馀把军队聚在井陉口，号称二十万。账面上兵力悬殊（赵军二十万是号称之数），难处在另一头：据赵营中李左车的分析，汉军是乘胜离国远斗，粮食势必落在后面。就在交手之前，他向陈馀递上一条非常具体的方案，方案没有被采纳。这一篇要说的就是这条被否掉的计，以及打赢之后，赢家怎样对待出计的人。
paras.en: Han Xin and Zhang Er were marching east with tens of thousands of troops, bound to attack the state of Zhao through Jingxing. King Xie of Zhao and the Lord of Cheng'an, Chen Yu, massed their forces at the Jingxing pass under a strength they claimed at two hundred thousand. On paper the gap was wide (Zhao's two hundred thousand was a claimed figure). The trouble lay elsewhere: as Li Zuoche, in the Zhao camp, saw it, the Han army was riding its victories far from home, and its grain was bound to fall behind. Before the two sides came to blows, he put a very specific plan to Chen Yu, and the plan was turned down. This piece is about that rejected proposal, and about how the winner treated the man who drew it up once the fighting was over.

heading.zh: 一边是锋不可当，一边是粮食在后
heading.en: An edge no one can stop, and grain trailing behind

paras.zh: 先看韩信这支部队的处境。据《淮阴侯列传》所记，李左车对成安君陈述汉军的来路：韩信涉西河、虏魏王、禽夏说，又在阏与打过硬仗，如今加上张耳，议欲下赵，这是乘胜而离国远斗，「其鋒不可當」。但同一段里他又算了另一笔账：千里运粮，士有饥色，砍了柴再做饭，部队不能常饱；井陉这条路车不能并轨、骑兵不能成列，行军数百里，粮食一定落在后面。优势和软肋是同一支军队的两面。
paras.en: Start with what Han Xin's army was up against. In the "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin," one chapter of Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, Li Zuoche — the Lord of Guangwu — traces the Han army's road to Zhao: Han Xin crossed the Western River, captured the King of Wei, took Xia Yue alive, and fought a bloody battle at Yuyu; with Zhang Er now beside him he means to bring down Zhao. This is an army riding its victories far from home, and its edge, in his words, cannot be withstood. But Li Zuoche keeps a second ledger in the same breath: grain hauled a thousand li leaves soldiers with hunger on their faces; you cut firewood before you can cook, and no army stays fed. On the Jingxing road two carts cannot run abreast and cavalry cannot form a column; after several hundred li, the supplies must be somewhere behind. Strength and frailty were two faces of one army.

paras.zh: 李左车给出的方案因此很具体：请拨奇兵三万人，抄小路断掉汉军辎重；主力深沟高垒，坚守不出战。汉军向前无仗可打、后退无路可走，后路被断、野外无处征粮，他估计不至十日，「兩將之頭可致於戲下」。他最后还留了一句警告：否则，「必爲二子所禽矣」——必定会被这两个人擒住。
paras.en: His proposal followed from that. He asked to be lent a surprise force of thirty thousand to cut the Han baggage train by the side roads, while the main body held behind deep ditches and high walls and refused battle. Ahead the Han would have no one to fight; behind them no way back; with their rear cut and nothing to forage in the open country, he reckoned that in less than ten days the heads of the two generals could be delivered to the commander's tent. He closed with a warning: otherwise, he said, you will surely be taken by those two.

paras.zh: 赵国这边的主帅成安君陈馀，本传在记他拒计时对他有这样一句定性：「儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。他拒绝的理由也被记了下来，可以分成三层：一是算术，兵法说十倍可以围、倍数可以战，韩信号称数万、其实不过数千，千里奔袭已经疲惫到极点；二是往后，如果这样还避而不击，以后来了更强的敌人又怎么应付；三是名声，那样「則諸侯謂吾怯，而輕來伐我」。他没有采纳广武君的计策。
paras.en: Chen Yu, the Lord of Cheng'an and Zhao's commander-in-chief, is characterized in this biography, at the point where he refuses the plan, as a Confucian who always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. His grounds for refusing are recorded too, and they fall into three layers. One is arithmetic: the manual says ten-to-one besieges, two-to-one fights; Han Xin claims tens of thousands but has no more than a few thousand, and a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone. The second looks ahead: if he avoided battle like this, how would he meet a stronger enemy that came later? The third is reputation: in his words roughly, the lords would then think him cowardly and come lightly to attack him. He did not take the Guangwu Jun's advice.

heading.zh: 从两千面红旗到一千金
heading.en: From two thousand red banners to a thousand in gold

paras.zh: 韩信先派人暗中探看，得知那条计没被采用，探子回报，他「大喜」，这才敢引兵下井陉，在离井陉口三十里处宿营。到夜半，他选出轻骑二千人，每人带一面红旗，抄小路到山上隐蔽观察赵军，并交代任务：赵军见我军退走，必然全营出动追击，你们就迅速进营，拔掉赵旗，插上汉军的红旗。这支骑兵此后的全部作用，取决于一个前提——赵军真的会倾巢而出。
paras.en: Han Xin sent men to spy out the camp and learned the plan had not been adopted. When they reported back, he was overjoyed, and only then did he dare lead his army down toward Jingxing, halting thirty li short of the pass. At midnight he chose two thousand light cavalry, each man carrying a red banner, and sent them by side paths to hide in the hills and watch the Zhao army, telling them that when Zhao saw the Han withdraw, it would empty its camp to pursue; they were then to go in fast, pull down the Zhao banners and stand up Han's red banners in their place. Everything this detachment did later hung on one premise — that the Zhao army really would come out.

paras.zh: 韩信先令裨将传飧，说「今日破趙會食」，诸将都不信，只假意应诺。他对军吏解释：赵军已先占据便利之地筑营，在没见到我军大将旗鼓之前，不肯攻击前军，怕我军走到险阻处就退回去。韩信于是派一万人先行而出，背靠河水列阵。赵军望见，「大笑」。按诸将事后引用的兵法，布阵要右背山陵、前左水泽。作者推测，背水列阵违背了这条常规，赵军或因此发笑；但原文只记了大笑，没有说他们笑什么。
paras.en: Han Xin first had his lieutenants pass round a light meal, announcing that they would eat together that day once Zhao was broken. None of the generals believed it; they feigned assent. He explained to his officers that Zhao had already built its camp on favorable ground and, until it saw the general's banners and drums, would not attack the vanguard, for fear that he would turn back on reaching the difficult ground. He then sent ten thousand men ahead; they went out and formed up with their backs to the river. The Zhao army saw them and roared with laughter. By the manual his generals later quoted, a proper line kept hills at the right rear and water at the left front. The author's guess is that this breach of the rule is what drew the laughter; the text records only that they laughed, not why.

paras.zh: 平旦，韩信打出大将的旗鼓，擂鼓出井陉口，赵军开营出击，双方打了很久。然后韩信、张耳假装丢下旗鼓（原文「詳弃鼓旗」），退向水边的部队；水上那一军把他们放入阵中，回身再战。赵军果然全营出动，争抢汉军的旗鼓，一路追击韩信、张耳。而已退入水边阵中的汉军人人殊死作战，打不垮。
paras.en: At dawn Han Xin raised the general's banners, beat the drums, and came out through the pass. The Zhao camp opened and attacked, and the fighting went on a long time. Then Han Xin and Zhang Er made a show of abandoning their drums and standards and fell back toward the force by the water, which opened its ranks to take them in and turned to fight again. The Zhao army duly poured out of its walls, scrambling for the Han drums and standards, chasing Han Xin and Zhang Er. The Han soldiers at the riverbank, Han Xin and Zhang Er now among them, fought to the death and could not be broken.

paras.zh: 埋伏的二千轻骑等的就是这一刻：赵营空了，他们驰入营垒，拔掉赵旗，插上二千面汉军红旗。赵军在前面不能取胜、又抓不到韩信，想回营时，看到的是「壁皆漢赤幟」，大惊，以为汉军已经把赵王和将领都拿下了，队伍顿时乱了，将领杀人弹压也止不住。汉军前后夹击，大破赵军，斩成安君于泜水上，擒赵王歇。
paras.en: The ambush had been waiting for exactly that. With the Zhao camp emptied, the two thousand riders swept in, pulled down the Zhao banners and raised two thousand red ones of Han. Unable to win in front and unable to catch Han Xin, the Zhao troops turned for their camp and found the walls all hung with Han's red banners. Greatly alarmed, they believed the Han had already taken the king of Zhao and his generals. The army dissolved; commanders cut men down to hold the line and could not. The Han struck from both sides, routed the Zhao army, killed the Lord of Cheng'an on the banks of the Zhi, and took King Xie alive.

paras.zh: 然后是这一篇真正关心的那一幕。韩信下令军中不得杀害广武君李左车，能活捉者赏千金。于是有人把捆着的李左车送到帐下，韩信亲自给他解开绳索，请他东向而坐、自己西向相对，以师礼待他。一支军队刚刚获胜，主帅下的命令里有一条，是保住对方那位出主意的人，还为此悬赏千金。
paras.en: Then comes the scene this piece is really about. Han Xin ordered that the Guangwu Jun, Li Zuoche, must not be killed, and set a thousand in gold on bringing him in alive. Someone delivered him bound to headquarters; Han Xin untied him, seated him facing east while he himself sat facing west, and treated him as his teacher. An army had just won, and among the commander-in-chief's orders was one to keep the other side's adviser alive — with a reward of a thousand in gold for it.

paras.zh: 庆功时诸将问了一个问题：兵法说布阵要右背山陵、前左水泽，将军却令我们背水列阵，还说破赵后会食，我们本来不服气，可居然胜了，这是什么术？韩信的回答是：这也在兵法里，只是诸位没细看，兵法不是说「陷之死地而後生，置之亡地而後存」吗？他说自己统带的不是长期抚循的旧部，是所谓「驅市人而戰之」，形势上非得把他们放进死地，让人人为自己的性命而战；若给他们留了生路，就全都跑了，还怎么用。诸将服气。
paras.en: At the celebration the generals asked a question. The manual says to keep hills at the right rear and water at the left front; you ordered us to form up with our backs to the water, and said we would eat after Zhao was broken. We were not convinced — yet we won. What art is this? Han Xin's answer: it is in the manual; you simply failed to see it there. Does it not say that men thrown onto death ground will live, and men placed where destruction is certain will survive? The men I have are not old followers I have cared for over the years; this is what is called driving men of the marketplace to fight. The situation demanded putting them on death ground, so that every man fought for his own life; give them ground to live in and they would all run, and then what use would they be? The generals conceded the point.

paras.zh: 接着韩信向李左车请教：我想北攻燕、东伐齐，怎样才能成功？李左车推辞，说自己是败军之将、亡国之臣，不足以议大事。韩信举了百里奚的例子：百里奚在虞国而虞亡，在秦国而秦霸，不是他在虞就笨、在秦就聪明，而是「用與不用，聽與不聽也」。他接着说，如果成安君听了您的计，我已经被擒了；正因为没有用您，我才有机会在此陪坐请教。
paras.en: Han Xin then asked Li Zuoche: I mean to strike Yan in the north and Qi in the east — how do I make that work? Li Zuoche declined: a defeated general cannot speak of courage, a minister of a ruined state cannot plan survival; what am I, a captured and ruined man, to weigh great matters with? Han Xin offered the story of Baili Xi, who saw Yu fall while he served Yu and saw Qin rise to hegemony while he served Qin: not that he was foolish at Yu and wise at Qin, but that his advice was used or not used, heeded or not heeded. And had the Lord of Cheng'an heeded your plan, a man like me would already have been taken. It is because he did not use you that I sit here asking.

paras.zh: 原文又记李左车说：「智者千慮，必有一失；愚者千慮，必有一得」，所以有句话说，狂夫之言，圣人也从中择取。这句话不是结局，而是献计前的铺垫：他接着说担心自己的计未必足用，但愿效愚忠，随即举成安君为例——有百战百胜之计，却「一旦而失之」，军败身死；然后献上自己的方案：按兵休整、镇抚赵地，再派辩士送信到燕国，向燕显示己方所长，并说「兵固有先聲而後實者」。韩信说「善」，「從其策」，派使者去燕，燕国「從風而靡」。一种解读是：他刚说的智者之失，紧接着就落在成安君身上；而韩信对出计者的对待，最后不只是礼遇，而是实际采用了他的计。
paras.en: The text also records Li Zuoche saying that the wise man, in a thousand considerations, must have one failure, and the fool, in a thousand considerations, must have one success — hence the saying, the sage still picks through a madman's words. This was not the end but the preface to a plan. He went on to say he feared his plan might not be adequate but wished to offer his humble loyalty, and pointed to the Lord of Cheng'an, who had a plan that could win a hundred battles out of a hundred and lost it at a stroke, his army beaten and himself killed. Then he laid out his own proposal: rest the troops, settle Zhao, and send a persuader with a letter to Yan displaying Han's strengths, since in war there are times when reputation comes first and substance after. Han Xin said, Good, followed his plan, and sent an envoy to Yan; Yan bent like grass before the wind. One reading: the failure of the wise man he had just spoken of falls at once on the Lord of Cheng'an; and Han Xin's treatment of the adviser ended not merely in courtesy but in actually adopting his plan.

heading.zh: 被否决的理由，赢在何处的解释
heading.en: Why the plan was refused, and how the win gets explained

paras.zh: 把原文所记陈馀拒绝的理由拆开看，会发现它们不是一类东西。「兵號數萬，其實不過數千」「千里而襲我，亦已罷極」是对敌情的判断，可以争论；「後有大者，何以加之」既不完全是对眼前汉军的判断，也不完全是形象问题，而是对以后局面的预想；“避而不击，诸侯就会说我怯懦”则不是对汉军的判断，是对自身形象的判断。此外，史家在记这些理由之前，先交代了他平日的立场：「常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。这是司马迁对他一贯说法的描述，不是他这一次拒绝时给出的理由；而且它不是判断，是一条规矩。一种解释是：这条规矩与李左车的奇兵之计正好相冲，二者或有关联，但原文并没有把它记为这次拒绝的理由。作者推断，这也是为什么原文要给陈馀加上「儒者也」这个身份标签——史家记的是立场，不只是失策。
paras.en: Split apart the reasons the text records for Chen Yu's refusal and they are not the same kind of thing. Claims tens of thousands, really no more than a few thousand; a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone — those are readings of the enemy, contestable in principle. If we avoid battle now, how will we meet a stronger enemy later is neither wholly a reading of the Han army in front of him nor wholly a matter of image; it is a projection about situations to come. Refuse battle and the lords will think me cowardly is not a reading of the Han army at all; it is a reading of his own image. Before recording those reasons, the historian also sets out his habitual stance: he always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. That is Sima Qian's description of what Chen Yu habitually said, not a reason he gave for this refusal; and it is not a judgment at all but a rule. One explanation: that rule runs directly against Li Zuoche's surprise-force plan, and the two may be connected, but the text does not record it as a ground for this refusal. The author's inference is that this is why the text labels Chen Yu a Confucian: the historian is recording a stance, not merely a mistake.

paras.zh: 第二个细节值得盯住：韩信并非胸有成竹地长驱直入，他是「使人閒視，知其不用」之后才敢进兵的。换句话说，那条没被采纳的计，是他的作战前提之一；两千轻骑的得手取决于赵军倾巢逐利，万人背水是另一重安排，而作者推断，赵军倾巢逐利这个条件只在李左车之计被弃后才成立。一种解释是，情报在这场胜负里的分量不低于阵法：韩信先确认了对手不会听对的意见，然后才把自己放进战场。
paras.en: Second detail worth holding onto: Han Xin did not march in on confidence. He advanced only after sending men to spy on the Zhao side and learning the plan had not been used. The rejected proposal was, in other words, one of the premises of his battle. The two thousand riders' success depended on the Zhao army emptying its camp to chase; the ten thousand men with the river at their backs were a separate arrangement. The author's inference is that this condition held only because Li Zuoche's plan had been shelved. One explanation: intelligence carried as much weight in this victory as formation. Han Xin first confirmed that his opponent would not listen to sound advice, then placed himself on the field.

paras.zh: 还有一个容易被忽略的不对称。战后诸将问的是“为什么背水”，也就是问赢家的招数妙在哪里；在诸将战后问答这一段里，没有人问“那条计当初为什么没被采纳”。作者推断，复盘天然聚光在胜者的技巧上，因为技巧可学；而一次否决看上去毫无技术含量，也不产生任何战果。可作者认为，这场仗里决定性的动作恰恰发生在开战之前——一次拒绝，和一次对拒绝的探知。
paras.en: There is also an easy-to-miss asymmetry. After the battle the generals asked why the backs-to-the-water formation — a question about what made the winner's move clever. In the generals' post-battle exchange as recorded, no one asks why that plan had not been adopted before the fighting. The author's inference: after-action review naturally spotlights the winner's technique, because technique can be learned, while a veto looks like it takes no skill and yields no result. Yet in the author's view, the decisive acts in this battle happened before the first blow fell — a refusal, and the discovery of that refusal.

paras.zh: 韩信本人把结论说得比谁都直白：他借百里奚的例子说，关键在「用與不用，聽與不聽也」，并说若成安君听足下计，我已经被擒。需要说清楚的是，这是韩信自己事后的说法，不是可以检验的事实；战场没有第二次。作者提出的替代情形是：如果陈馀采纳李左车之计、坚壁不出并断其辎重，韩信会怎么改，史书没有记载，任何人都只能推测。可以确认的是：韩信的部署以赵军会追出来为条件；至于赵军追出来与那条计被否决之间的关系有多直接，是作者的推断。
paras.en: Han Xin put the conclusion more bluntly than anyone: speaking of Baili Xi, he said it turned on whether a man is used or not, heeded or not, and that had the Lord of Cheng'an listened to you, I would be the captive. To be clear, that is Han Xin's own account after the event, not a fact anyone can check; battles are not run twice. The alternative the author raises: had Chen Yu adopted the plan, held his walls and cut the supplies, what Han Xin would have done instead is unrecorded and can only be guessed at. What can be established is that his deployment depended on the Zhao army coming out to chase; how directly that depended on the plan's rejection is the author's inference.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景之一：一家小店打算在旺季前大批备货，整套计划的前提是供应商不会临时涨价。动手之前先打一个电话把这个前提问清楚，比事后懊悔有用。韩信是先派人探知李左车的计策没被采用，才敢进兵的；他的胆子建立在一次确认上。
paras.en: First modern scene, fictional: a small shop plans to stock up heavily before the busy season, and the whole plan rests on the supplier not raising prices at the last minute. One phone call to check that assumption before buying is worth more than regret afterwards. Han Xin advanced only after his scouts confirmed that Li Zuoche's plan had been turned down; his boldness rested on a check.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景之二：一次交接。竞标赢了之后，甲方请的顾问，偏偏是对方阵营里那位方案被否的人——不是羞辱，是把他的思路当成课程。当年韩信解缚、师事李左车，做的就是这件事：赢家最值得问的，常常不是自己的谋士，而是对手那边没被听的那个。
paras.en: Second modern scene, fictional: a handover. Having won the bid, the client hires as consultant precisely the person on the losing side whose plan was voted down — not to humiliate him, but to treat his thinking as coursework. Untying the bonds and serving Li Zuoche as a teacher is exactly that: the person most worth asking is often not your own adviser, but the one on the other side who went unheard.

heading.en: How far this piece can be certain

paras.zh: 本文所有事实都来自司马迁《史记·淮阴侯列传》一篇，本文没有使用第二个史源作交叉验证。也就是说，李左车的算粮、陈馀的理由、诸将的疑问、李左车的谦辞，都出自同一作者的记述；对话是史书的记述，未必是现场的逐字原话，本文使用其中原句处，只取原文中确有的文字。
paras.en: Every fact here comes from one text, Sima Qian's "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin"; this piece uses no second source to cross-check against. Li Zuoche's supply arithmetic, Chen Yu's reasons, the generals' questions, Li Zuoche's modesty — all of it is a single author's record. The speeches are the historian's account and need not be verbatim transcripts; where this piece uses the original wording, it takes only phrasing actually present in the text.

paras.zh: 还有两处必须留白。第一，「誠令成安君聽足下計，若信者亦已爲禽矣」是韩信本人事后的说法，无法检验，本文只把它当作韩信的自我解释来记，不当作事实。第二，陈馀的想法，本文严格按原文所记的理由写，不替他补充任何心理活动；至于他若采纳那条计会怎样，是作者提出的分析情形，不是记录，也永远不会有答案。
paras.en: Two things must stay open. First, Han Xin's statement that, had the Lord of Cheng'an heeded Li Zuoche's plan, a man like him would already have been taken is his own claim after the event, untestable; this piece records it as his explanation of himself, not as fact. Second, where Chen Yu's mind is concerned, this piece follows exactly the reasons the text gives and adds nothing; what would have happened had he adopted the plan is an analytical counterfactual the author offers, not a record, and it will never have an answer.

scenario.zh: 项目评审会上，有人提议暂缓扩张、先加固后方（相当于“深沟高垒、坚壁不战”）；主事者否决，理由有两条：一是“这么做会被对手看轻、以为我们怕了”，二是“我们做事讲正道，不玩这种取巧”。
scenario.en: At a project review, someone proposes pausing expansion to reinforce the rear — the equivalent of "dig in behind high walls and refuse battle." The person in charge turns it down on two grounds: first, "doing that will make rivals think we are afraid"; second, "we play straight; we don't do clever tricks."

question.zh: 当拒绝一条建议的主要理由是“采纳它会显得我们示弱”或“这不像我们做事的风格”时，你怎样分辨哪些话是对情势的判断、哪些只是表态？如果想让这类建议至少得到一次认真的检验，你会在会前改变什么？
question.en: When the main grounds for rejecting a proposal are "adopting it would make us look weak" or "that is not how we do things," how do you tell which words are judgments about the situation and which are declarations of identity? And if you want such a proposal to get at least one serious test, what would you change before the meeting?

assumptions.zh:
双方掌握的公开信息大致相当
否决者拥有最终决定权
短期内没有第三方裁判能判定谁对
assumptions.en:
Both sides hold roughly the same public information
The person rejecting the proposal has final decision authority
No third party will settle in the short term who is right

steps.zh:
把拒绝理由拆成两栏：“它是否有效”与“它是否体面”，逐条标注依据
请提出者给出最短验证路径：几天内、出现什么信号就说明方案确实不成立
把这次否决写进记录，注明当时依据的理由和预期，约好回看的日期
steps.en:
Split the grounds for rejection into two columns — does it work, and does it look right — and mark what each ground rests on
Ask the proposer for the shortest verification path: within a few days, what signal would show the proposal really does not hold up?
Put the rejection on record, noting the reasons and expectations at the time, and agree on a date to look back at it

alternative.zh: 另一种做法（作者提出）：先不争论方案本身，先换取信息——正如韩信「使人閒視」，先确认对方会不会真的照那条路走，再决定自己进退。
alternative.en: Another approach, proposed by the author: set the merits of the proposal aside first and buy information instead — as Han Xin sent men to spy on the Zhao camp, confirm whether the other side will actually take that route before deciding your own advance or retreat.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文唯一史源为司马迁《史记·淮阴侯列传》。其中人物对话是史家记述，未必逐字；「誠令成安君聽足下計，若信者亦已爲禽矣」出自韩信之口，属事后自述，不可检验。除原文所记理由外，本文未对陈馀的心理作任何补充；作者提出的替代情形只用于分析，不作事实陈述。
uncertainty_note.en: The only historical source for this piece is Sima Qian's "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin" in the Records of the Grand Historian. The speeches there are the historian's account and need not be verbatim; the statement that, had the Lord of Cheng'an heeded Li Zuoche's plan, a man like Han Xin would already have been taken comes from Han Xin's own mouth, an after-the-fact statement that cannot be tested. Beyond the reasons recorded in the original text, this piece adds nothing to Chen Yu's psychology; the alternative scenario the author offers serves analysis only and is not stated as fact.

preheader.zh: 一条被拒绝的建议、两千面红旗，和一句“用与不用，听与不听”。
preheader.en: A rejected plan, two thousand red flags, and a lesson about listening.

what.zh: 井陉之战一段在中前部，从“信與張耳以兵數萬”读起。
what.en: The Jingxing passage is in the first half; start from 信與張耳以兵數萬.
